'''Massimilla "Milla" Baldo Ceolin''' (12 August 1924, [[Legnago]], Italy – 25 November 2011) was an Italian [[particle physicist]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Faces and places: Milla Baldo Ceolin 1924–2011|journal=CERN Courier|date=March 2012|volume=52|issue=2|page=38|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734768}}</ref>
 
She was the daughter of the owner of a small mechanical workshop.<ref name=":0" />

==Education and academic history==

Milla Baldo Ceolin attended the Liceo Classico (classical high school) in [[Legnago]], in the province of [[Verona]], and obtained her high school diploma (maturità) in 1943. At the end of the [[Second world War|Second World War]], she enrolled in the physics degree program at the University of Padua, where she obtained her master's degree in 1952.

At the Physics Institute, Milla Baldo met Carlo Ceolin, a theoretical physicist, who accompanied her throughout her entire life. In 1953, Milla became Mrs. Baldo Ceolin.

Milla Baldo Ceolin obtained the chair of "Fisica Superiore" in 1963, the first woman to hold a chair at the [[University of Padua]] since its founding in 1222.

In Padua, from 1965 to 1968, she served as Head of the local section of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] (INFN), and from 1973 to 1978 as Head of the Physics Institute.

Since 1998, she has been Professor Emeritus at the University of Padua.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Peruzzi |first=Giulio |date=2011-12-08 |title=Milla Baldo Ceolin, la signora dei neutrini |url=https://www.scienzainrete.it/contenuto/articolo/milla-baldo-ceolin-signora-dei-neutrini |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Scienza in rete |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Baldo-Ceolin,_Milla@960123456.html |title=CWP at physics.UCLA.edu // Milla Baldo-Ceolin |publisher=Cwp.library.ucla.edu |date=1992-03-13 |accessdate=2014-03-06}}</ref>

==Career and research==

In the 1950s, her research focused on the study of cosmic ray interactions in nuclear emulsions, which were exposed at high-altitude mountain laboratories or carried by balloon experiments. This activity culminated in the G-stack experiment,<ref>Belloni, Lanfranco; Dilworth, Constance (1988). "From little to big. A story of European postwar collaboration with nuclear emulsions". In De Maria, Michelangelo; Grilli, Mario; Sebastiani, Fabio (ed.). The restructuring of Physical Sciences in Europe and the United States 1945–1960. World Scientific. pp. 732–744.</ref> a large international collaboration that provided the first indications of [[strange particle]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Peruzzi |first1=Giulio |last2=Talas |first2=Sofia |date=May 2007 |title=The Italian contributions to cosmic-ray physics from Bruno Rossi to the G-Stack. A new window into the inexhaustible wealth of nature |journal=[[La Rivista del Nuovo Cimento]] |volume=30 |issue=5 |pages=197–257 |url=https://www.sif.it/riviste/sif/ncr/econtents/2007/030/05/article/0 |language=en |doi=10.1393/ncr/i2007-10020-0}}
</ref> According to her own words: "Research groups emerging from the catastrophe of the war had little more than their enthusiasm to contribute at the forefront of physics research, but by using the [[nuclear emulsion]] technique, they were able to disclose phenomena whose existence no one had suspected."<ref>{{Cite journal
|last = Baldo Ceolin
|first = Milla
|date = 2002
|title = The Discreet Charm of the Nuclear Emulsion Era
|journal = Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science
|volume = 52
|pages = 1–21
|doi = 10.1146/annurev.nucl.52.050102.090730
|issn = 0163-8998
}}</ref>

In 1958,  she published the discovery of the anti-Lambda [[hyperon]], by exposing nuclear emulsions to a proton beam produced at the [[Bevatron|Berkeley Bevatron]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Prowse |first=D. J. |last2=Baldo-Ceolin |first2=M. |date=1958-09-01 |title=Anti-Lambda Hyperon |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.179 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=1 |issue=5 |pages=179–180 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.179 |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> The discovery of the anti-Lambda (the first anti-hyperon ever observed) was highly significant: Milla Baldo Ceolin conceived the experiment, performed the feasibility calculations, and correctly interpreted the event observed in the photographic plates exposed at the Bevatron. This result provided the first evidence of antimatter carrying strangeness.<ref>{{Cite journal
|last1 = Ricci
|first1 = Renato Angelo
|last2 = Puglierin
|first2 = Gabriele
|date = 2011
|title = Milla Baldo-Ceolin (1924-2011)
|journal = Il Nuovo Saggiatore
|publisher = Società Italiana di Fisica
|volume = 27
|issue = 5–6
|pages = 105–106
|url = https://static.sif.it/SIF/resources/public/files/ricordo/baldoceolin.pdf
|format = PDF
|language = it
|access-date = 2026-06-06
}}
</ref>

Her research then focused on charged and neutral [[K mesons]], first using nuclear emulsions and subsequently with [[bubble chamber]]s at the  Lawrence [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Berkeley National Laboratory]], at [[CERN]], and at [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics|ITEP]] in [[Moscow]]. Her work produced important results on quantum numbers, selection rules, and fundamental invariances, including tests of  [[CPT symmetry]] from the study of K⁰ meson decays in the Xenon bubble chamber at ITEP.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Barmin |first=V. V. |last2=Barylov |first2=V. G. |last3=Chuvilo |first3=I. V. |last4=Davidenko |first4=G. V. |last5=Demidov |first5=V. S. |last6=Dolgolenko |first6=A. G. |last7=Meshkovsky |first7=A. G. |last8=Okun |first8=L. B. |last9=Shebanov |first9=V. A. |last10=Baldo-Ceolin |first10=M. |last11=Calimani |first11=E. |last12=Ciampolillo |first12=S. |last13=Mattioli |first13=F. |last14=Miari |first14=G. |last15=Sconza |first15=A. |date=1984-12-10 |title=CPT symmetry and neutral kaons |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0550321384905510 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=247 |issue=2 |pages=293–312 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(84)90551-0 |issn=0550-3213|display-authors=1}}</ref>

In the 1970s, she turned to [[neutrino]] physics. Soon after the discovery of [[weak neutral current]]s by the [[Gargamelle]] collaboration at CERN,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1973-09-03 |title=Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the gargamelle neutrino experiment |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269373904991 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=138–140 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(73)90499-1 |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> she proposed the NUE experiment at CERN, to firmly confirm the discovery of neutral weak leptonic currents. The experiment used [[spark chamber]]s to detect the [[elastic scattering]] of neutrinos and antineutrinos on electrons, providing evidence of neutral weak leptonic currents and determining a value for the [[Weinberg angle]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Faissner |first=H. |last2=Fasold |first2=H. G. |last3=Frenzel |first3=E. |last4=Hansl |first4=T. |last5=Hoffmann |first5=D. |last6=Maull |first6=K. |last7=Radermacher |first7=E. |last8=Reithler |first8=H. |last9=de Witt |first9=H. |last10=Baldo-Ceolin |first10=M. |last11=Bobisut |first11=F. |last12=Huzita |first12=H. |last13=Loreti |first13=M. |last14=Puglierin |first14=G. |last15=Scotoni |first15=I. |date=1978-07-24 |title=Measurement of Muon-Neutrino and -Antineutrino Scattering off Electrons |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.41.213 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=213–216 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.41.213 |issn=0031-9007|display-authors=1}}</ref>  She subsequently  participated  in a series of experiments at the [[BEBC]] bubble chamber at CERN, filled with [[deuterium]], including PS180, which established one of the first experimental limits on [[neutrino oscillation]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1986-10-23 |title=New experimental limits on νμ→νe oscillations |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269386905861 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=179 |issue=3 |pages=307–312 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(86)90586-1 |issn=0370-2693}}</ref>

Following the publications on [[Grand Unified Theory|Grand Unified Theories]] in the early 1980s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Georgi |first=Howard |last2=Glashow |first2=S. L. |date=1974-02-25 |title=Unity of All Elementary-Particle Forces |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=32 |issue=8 |pages=438–441 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438 |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> she began planning experiments to search for one of their original predictions: the possible existence of [[neutron-antineutron oscillations]]. She proposed, designed and realized a series of two experiments on free neutrons generated at the [[nuclear reactor]] of the [[Institut Laue–Langevin|Institut Laue-Langevin]]  at [[Grenoble]]. The first experiment established the earliest experimental bound on the neutron-antineutron oscillation time,  <math>\tau_{n\bar{n}} \geq 10^6</math> s,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1985-06-13 |title=Experimental search for neutron-antineutron transitions with free neutrons |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/037026938591367X |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=156 |issue=1-2 |pages=122–128 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(85)91367-X |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> while the second, with an upgraded setup, pushed the limit to <math>\tau_{n\bar{n}} \geq 0.84 \times 10^8</math> s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Baldo-Ceolin |first=M. |last2=Benetti |first2=P. |last3=Bitter |first3=T. |last4=Bobisut |first4=F. |last5=Calligarich |first5=E. |last6=Dolfini |first6=R. |last7=Dubbers |first7=D. |last8=El-Muzeini |first8=P. |last9=Genoni |first9=M. |last10=Gibin |first10=D. |last11=Gigli Berzolari |first11=A. |last12=Gobrecht |first12=K. |last13=Guglielmi |first13=A. |last14=Last |first14=J. |last15=Laveder |first15=M. |display-authors=1 |date=1994-09-01 |title=A new experimental limit on neutron-antineutron oscillations |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01580321 |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik C Particles and Fields |language=en |volume=63 |issue=3 |pages=409–416 |doi=10.1007/BF01580321 |issn=1431-5858}}</ref> the best experimental limit for free neutrons published to date.

Afterwards she led the italian contribution to  the WA96/NOMAD (Neutrino Oscillation MAgnetic Detector) experiment, which aimed to search for <math>\nu_\mu-\nu_\tau</math> oscillations using high-energy neutrinos (predominantly ν<sub>μ</sub>) from the [[Super Proton Synchrotron|CERN SPS]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1998-02-11 |title=The NOMAD experiment at the CERN SPS |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168900297010796 |journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment |volume=404 |issue=1 |pages=96–128 |doi=10.1016/S0168-9002(97)01079-6 |issn=0168-9002}}</ref> The experiment was motivated by the anomaly in the measured flux of [[Atmospheric neutrino oscillation|atmospheric neutrinos]] reported by [[Super-Kamiokande|KamiokaNDE]]<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1988-04-28 |title=Experimental study of the atmospheric neutrino flux |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269388916905 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=205 |issue=2-3 |pages=416–420 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(88)91690-5 |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> and by theoretical speculations about the possibility that the heaviest neutrino could be the [[hot dark matter]] component.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1992-10-08 |title=The prospects for CHORUS and NOMAD in the light of COBE and GALLEX |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/037026939290629I |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=292 |issue=1-2 |pages=189–194 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(92)90629-I |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> In the same years (1998), evidence for <math>\nu_\mu-\nu_\tau</math> oscillations was reported by the Super-Kamiokande experiment,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fukuda |first=Y. |last2=Hayakawa |first2=T. |last3=Ichihara |first3=E. |last4=Inoue |first4=K. |last5=Ishihara |first5=K. |last6=Ishino |first6=H. |last7=Itow |first7=Y. |last8=Kajita |first8=T. |last9=Kameda |first9=J. |last10=Kasuga |first10=S. |last11=Kobayashi |first11=K. |last12=Kobayashi |first12=Y. |last13=Koshio |first13=Y. |last14=Miura |first14=M. |last15=Nakahata |first15=M. |display-authors=1 |date=1998-08-24 |title=Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.1562 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=81 |issue=8 |pages=1562–1567 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.1562 |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> with oscillation parameters not accessible to the NOMAD experiment. [[Takaaki Kajita]] was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 2015 for this discovery.    [[File:Baldo Ceolin and Ray Davis.jpg|right|thumb|350px|Milla Baldo Ceolin and Nobel laureate [[Raymond Davis Jr.|Ray Davis]] at the Neutrino Telescopes Workshop, Istituto Veneto di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti, Venice, 1990]]

Eventually, she joined the [[ICARUS (experiment)|ICARUS experiment]],<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2004-07-21 |title=Design, construction and tests of the ICARUS T600 detector |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168900204004966 |journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment |language=en-US |volume=527 |issue=3 |pages=329–410 |doi=10.1016/j.nima.2004.02.044 |issn=0168-9002}}</ref>  a neutrino  experiment at the [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso|Gran Sasso National Laboratories]] (LNGS). It used a [[Time projection chamber|Time Projection Chamber]] filled with liquid [[argon]] (LAr-TPC), a technology developed by [[Carlo Rubbia]], containing about 600 tons of active argon mass. The experiment received the [[CNGS]] neutrino beam from CERN, 730&nbsp;km away.

In 1988, she initiated the series of [https://neutrino.pd.infn.it/ International Workshops on Neutrino Telescopes] at the [[Istituto Veneto di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Workshop: Neutrino telescopes|journal=CERN Courier|date=May 1990|volume=30|issue=4|pages=15–17|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1731770}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=CERN |date=2003-05-31 |title=Neutrinos: universal messengers at all scales |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/neutrinos-universal-messengers-at-all-scales/ |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards==
*Fellow of the [[Istituto Veneto di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti]], (since 1977), of the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] (since 1987); of the Accademia Galileiana di Padova (since 1966) and Accademia delle Scienze di Torino  (since 2008).
*1976: Awarded the [[Feltrinelli Prize]] by the [[Accademia dei Lincei]].
*1980: Gold Medal as "Benemeriti della Scuola, della Cultura e dell'Arte" by the Italian Ministero della Pubblica Istruzione.
*1984: Award of [[Italian Physical Society]] (SIF), for working in the field of weak interactions and getting outstanding physical results, in occasion of the 50th Anniversary of Fermi's Theory.
*1993: Gold Medal as "Benemeriti della Scienza e Cultura" by the Italian Ministero della Pubblica Istruzione.
*In 1995, she was included in the [[UCLA]] archive titled "Contributions of the 20th Century Women to Physics" ([http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/intro.html CWP]), a digital project created to document the major scientific achievements of female physicists (86 entries).
*2007: [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] of the Italian Physical Society "per gli importanti lavori sulla fisica dei mesoni K e sui neutrini".
*2012: The Department of Physics and Astronomy of the University and the Padova Division of INFN (National Institute of Nuclear Science) organized a symposium in her honor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tribute to Milla Baldo Ceolin |url=http://tribute-milla.fisica.unipd.it/index.html |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=tribute-milla.fisica.unipd.it}}</ref>
*In 2015, a biography was published.<ref>{{Cite book |title = Milla Baldo Ceolin|author = Nicolaci, Maria|publisher = Edizioni Asino d'oro|year = 2015|isbn = 9788864433189|language = Italian}}</ref>
*In 2021, [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]]  established the "Milla Baldo Ceolin" National Award  to the ten best master's theses in theoretical physics. The award aims to promote the visibility and growth of young female researchers in theoretical physics.
*2021: The Department of Physics and Astronomy of the University of Padua and the INFN Section of Padua commemorated Milla Baldo Ceolin,  whose studies and pioneering, visionary research opened new horizons for modern physics and for the understanding of the structure of the Universe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Giornate in ricordo di Milla Baldo Ceolin |url=https://agenda.infn.it/event/28884/overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260521015250/https://agenda.infn.it/event/28884/overview |archive-date=2026-05-21 |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Agenda (Indico) |language=en}}</ref>
*The "Milla Baldo Ceolin" nursery school opened in Padua in September 2021 with the support of the [https://fondazionecariparo.it/ Cariparo Foundation].
*In 2023, the students of the junior high school in Roncà, in the province of [[Verona]], celebrated the scientist from [[Legnago]], Massimilla Baldo Ceolin, choosing that their school should bear the name of the woman who, 60 years before, was the first to obtain a professorship at the University of Padua.<ref>{{Cite web  |date=2023-12-20 |title=I ragazzi decidono di intitolare la loro scuola alla scienziata pioniera della fisica |url=https://www.larena.it/territorio-veronese/est/medie-ronca-intitolate-massimilla-baldo-ceolin-1.10467947 |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=L'Arena |language=it}}</ref>
